title: Continuing Appropriations Act, 2027

claims.claim: Introduced by Rep. Tom Cole
claims.sourceSpan: Mr. Cole introduced the following bill
claims.note: Source names "Mr. Cole" as introducer; party/district (R-OK-4) is structural cache metadata, not in source.

claims.claim: the committee of referral is the House Appropriations Committee
claims.sourceSpan: referred to the Committee on Appropriations

claims.claim: Rep. Cole is Chair of the House Appropriations Committee
claims.note: Source states referral to the Committee on Appropriations but nowhere states Cole chairs it. Extrinsic role claim; kept structural but unsourced.

claims.claim: cleared by the House per the latest recorded action
claims.note: Backed by structural vote metadata (House Passed 220-205, 2026-07-21); not in the introduced source text but a recorded-vote structural fact permitted by the rubric.

claims.claim: has a hard December 4, 2026 expiration date
claims.sourceSpan: (3) December 4, 2026.

claims.claim: Short-term continuing resolutions are the standard vehicle Congress uses to avoid a shutdown and typically clear both chambers under time pressure
claims.note: Generic legislative-process characterization, not drawn from bill source. Structural but unsourced framing.

claims.claim: The IHS anomaly amounts, DC local-spending authority, and survivor payments are the most likely points of pushback in Senate negotiations
claims.note: The underlying provisions exist in source (Secs 123/119/127), but the prediction of Senate pushback is speculation, not sourced.

claims.claim: A short-term continuing resolution keeping the government funded at fiscal year 2026 rates and under fiscal year 2026 authorities
claims.sourceSpan: at a rate for operations as provided in the applicable appropriations Acts for fiscal year 2026 and under the authority and conditions provided in such Acts

claims.claim: funded from October 1, 2026 through December 4, 2026
claims.sourceSpan: (3) December 4, 2026.
claims.note: Dec 4, 2026 is Sec 106(3); the Oct 1, 2026 start is the FY2027 start ("for fiscal year 2027") and "October 1, 2026" appears verbatim in Sec 115.

claims.claim: covers all twelve regular appropriations areas
claims.sourceSpan: for which appropriations, funds, or other authority were made available in the following appropriations Acts:
claims.note: Sec 101(1)-(12) enumerate the 12 appropriations Acts.

claims.claim: buying Congress time to finish full-year fiscal year 2027 appropriations
claims.sourceSpan: The enactment into law of the applicable appropriations Act for fiscal year 2027 without any provision for such project or activity.

claims.claim: carries a small set of program-specific anomalies
claims.sourceSpan: In addition to amounts otherwise provided by section 101, amounts are provided for

claims.claim: extends the National Flood Insurance Program authority
claims.sourceSpan: Sections 1309(a) and 1319 of the National Flood Insurance Act of 1968 (42 U.S.C. 4016(a) and 4026) shall be applied by substituting the date specified in section 106(3) of this Act for

claims.claim: blocks the automatic Member of Congress cost-of-living adjustment during the covered period
claims.sourceSpan: no adjustment shall be made under section 601(a) of the Legislative Reorganization Act of 1946 (2 U.S.C. 4501) (relating to cost of living adjustments for Members of Congress) during the period covered by this Act
claims.note: "automatic" is a mild gloss (601(a) COLA is automatic); substance sourced.

claims.claim: Funds the federal government at fiscal year 2026 levels through December 4, 2026
claims.sourceSpan: at a rate for operations as provided in the applicable appropriations Acts for fiscal year 2026

claims.claim: extends a handful of expiring authorities including the National Flood Insurance Program
claims.sourceSpan: Sections 1309(a) and 1319 of the National Flood Insurance Act of 1968 (42 U.S.C. 4016(a) and 4026) shall be applied by substituting the date specified in section 106(3) of this Act for

claims.claim: Continues fiscal year 2026 rates and authorities into fiscal year 2027
claims.sourceSpan: at a rate for operations as provided in the applicable appropriations Acts for fiscal year 2026 and under the authority and conditions provided in such Acts

claims.claim: Covers all 12 regular appropriations areas (Ag, CJS, DoD, E&W, FSGG, DHS, Interior, Labor-HHS-Ed, Legislative, Milcon-VA, State, T-HUD)
claims.sourceSpan: The Agriculture, Rural Development, Food and Drug Administration, and Related Agencies Appropriations Act, 2026
claims.note: Sec 101 enumerates all 12 Acts; abbreviations map correctly to items (1)-(12).

claims.claim: Expires on December 4, 2026 or upon enactment of the underlying full-year Act, whichever comes first
claims.sourceSpan: shall be available until whichever of the following first occurs
claims.note: Source lists three first-to-occur triggers; the two-item phrasing is a faithful simplification (Dec 4 is the backstop).

claims.claim: No new production of items not funded for production in fiscal year 2026
claims.sourceSpan: the new production of items not funded for production in fiscal year 2026 or prior years

claims.claim: No production-rate increases above those sustained with fiscal year 2026 funds
claims.sourceSpan: the increase in production rates above those sustained with fiscal year 2026 funds

claims.claim: No new multi-year procurements using advance procurement funding for economic order quantity
claims.sourceSpan: initiate multi-year procurements utilizing advance procurement funding for economic order quantity procurement unless specifically appropriated later

claims.claim: Additional $75.77M for Indian Health Service — Indian Health Services facility staffing
claims.sourceSpan: at a rate for operations of $75,774,000, for an additional amount for costs of staffing and operating facilities that were opened, renovated, or expanded in fiscal years 2022, 2026, and 2027
claims.section: Sec. 123(a) — Indian Health Service--Indian Health Services
claims.note: $75,774,000 -> $75.77M; binds to Indian Health Services account.

claims.claim: Additional $8.30M for Indian Health Service — Indian Health Facilities staffing
claims.sourceSpan: at a rate for operations of $8,296,000, for an additional amount for costs of staffing and operating facilities that were opened, renovated, or expanded in fiscal years 2022, 2026, and 2027
claims.section: Sec. 123(b) — Indian Health Service--Indian Health Facilities
claims.note: $8,296,000 -> $8.30M; binds to Indian Health Facilities account.

claims.claim: WIC apportioned up to the rate necessary to maintain participation
claims.sourceSpan: apportioned at the rate for operations necessary to maintain participation
claims.note: Source says WIC "may be apportioned AT the rate ... necessary to maintain participation"; analysis says "UP TO the rate." "up to" imports a ceiling the WIC provision does not use (unlike Secs 118/122/125 which do say "up to"). Minor wording drift.

claims.claim: SBA business loan program apportioned up to the rate necessary for increased demand
claims.sourceSpan: may be apportioned up to the rate for operations necessary to accommodate increased demand for commitments for general business loans authorized under paragraphs (1) through (35) of section 7(a) of the Small Business Act

claims.claim: FEMA Disaster Relief Fund apportioned up to the rate necessary for response and recovery
claims.sourceSpan: may be apportioned up to the rate for operations necessary to carry out response and recovery activities under the Robert T. Stafford Disaster Relief and Emergency Assistance Act

claims.claim: National Flood Insurance Program (42 U.S.C. 4016(a) and 4026) extended through December 4, 2026
claims.sourceSpan: Sections 1309(a) and 1319 of the National Flood Insurance Act of 1968 (42 U.S.C. 4016(a) and 4026) shall be applied by substituting the date specified in section 106(3) of this Act for

claims.claim: Livestock Mandatory Reporting Act and Agricultural Marketing Act (7 U.S.C. 1636i, 1635 note) extended through December 4, 2026
claims.sourceSpan: Section 260 of the Agricultural Marketing Act of 1946 (7 U.S.C. 1636i) and section 942 of the Livestock Mandatory Reporting Act of 1999 (7 U.S.C. 1635 note; Public Law 106-78) shall be applied by substituting the date specified in section 106(3) of this Act for

claims.claim: TANF and Section 1108(b) of the Social Security Act continued through December 4, 2026
claims.sourceSpan: Activities authorized by part A of title IV (other than under section 403(c) or 418) and section 1108(b) of the Social Security Act shall continue through the date specified in section 106(3), in the manner authorized for fiscal year 2026
claims.note: TANF = part A of title IV of the Social Security Act.

claims.claim: $174,000 survivor payment to Alfredia Scott, widow of Rep. David A. Scott (D-GA)
claims.sourceSpan: for payment to Alfredia Scott, widow of David A. Scott, late a Representative from the State of Georgia, $174,000
claims.note: Name/$174,000/Representative/Georgia sourced; the "(D)" party letter is extrinsic cache metadata, not in source.

claims.claim: $174,000 payment to the heirs at law of Sen. Lindsey O. Graham (R-SC)
claims.sourceSpan: for payment to the heirs at law of Lindsey O. Graham, late a Senator from South Carolina, $174,000
claims.note: Name/$174,000/Senator/South Carolina sourced; "(R)" party letter is extrinsic metadata. Analysis correctly assigns "heirs at law" (Graham) vs "widow" (Scott).

claims.claim: Blocks the Member of Congress automatic cost-of-living adjustment during the covered period
claims.sourceSpan: no adjustment shall be made under section 601(a) of the Legislative Reorganization Act of 1946 (2 U.S.C. 4501) (relating to cost of living adjustments for Members of Congress) during the period covered by this Act

claims.claim: DC may expend local funds at the rate set in the Fiscal Year 2027 Local Budget Act of 2026 (Bill 26-0659)
claims.sourceSpan: at the rate set forth in the Fiscal Year 2027 Local Budget Act of 2026 (Bill 26-0659) as modified as of the date of enactment of this Act

claims.claim: Rate is modified as of the date of enactment of this Act
claims.sourceSpan: as modified as of the date of enactment of this Act

claims.claim: Continues fiscal year 2026 appropriations rates and authorities for continuing projects across the 12 regular appropriations acts through December 4, 2026
claims.sourceSpan: for continuing projects or activities (including the costs of direct loans and loan guarantees) that are not otherwise specifically provided for in this Act

claims.claim: Section 101 lists the 12 anchor appropriations acts and continues each at fiscal year 2026 rates
claims.sourceSpan: for which appropriations, funds, or other authority were made available in the following appropriations Acts:

claims.claim: Section 106 sets the expiration to whichever of three events occurs first: enactment of the applicable full-year FY2027 Act, enactment of a full-year Act without a provision for the covered activity, or December 4, 2026
claims.sourceSpan: appropriations and funds made available and authority granted pursuant to this Act shall be available until whichever of the following first occurs
claims.note: Three first-to-occur triggers preserved; item (1) in source is "enactment ... of an appropriation for any project or activity provided for in this Act" (paraphrased as "the applicable full-year FY2027 Act") — faithful gist.

claims.claim: Section 110 requires that only the most limited funding action permitted be used to continue projects
claims.sourceSpan: only the most limited funding action of that permitted in the Act shall be taken

claims.claim: Prohibits new starts, production increases, and new multi-year procurements at the Department of Defense during the continuing resolution period
claims.sourceSpan: No appropriation or funds made available or authority granted pursuant to section 101 for the Department of Defense shall be used for

claims.claim: Section 102 bars production not funded in FY2026, production-rate increases above FY2026 levels, or initiation of projects not previously funded; also bars new multi-year procurement using advance procurement funding for economic order quantity unless specifically appropriated later
claims.sourceSpan: the initiation, resumption, or continuation of any project, activity, operation, or organization

claims.claim: Provides IHS staffing anomalies of $75.77M for Indian Health Services and $8.30M for Indian Health Facilities to staff and operate facilities opened, renovated, or expanded in fiscal years 2022, 2026, and 2027
claims.sourceSpan: costs of staffing and operating facilities that were opened, renovated, or expanded in fiscal years 2022, 2026, and 2027

claims.claim: Section 123(a) provides $75.77M for Indian Health Service — Indian Health Services; Section 123(b) provides $8.30M for Indian Health Service — Indian Health Facilities; both apportioned up to the rate necessary to staff and operate the covered facilities
claims.sourceSpan: such amounts may be apportioned up to the rate for operations necessary to staff and operate such facilities

claims.claim: Extends the National Flood Insurance Program's authority through December 4, 2026 by substituting that date for the September 30, 2026 statutory expiration
claims.sourceSpan: shall be applied by substituting the date specified in section 106(3) of this Act for
claims.note: Struck date "September 30, 2026" appears verbatim in Sec 121.

claims.claim: Section 121 applies sections 1309(a) and 1319 of the National Flood Insurance Act of 1968; a retroactive-application clause treats the substitution as if in effect on September 30, 2026 if enacted after that date
claims.sourceSpan: If this Act is enacted after September 30, 2026, this section shall be applied as if it were in effect on September 30, 2026.

claims.claim: Continues SBA general business loan programs, FEMA Disaster Relief Fund response and recovery, and Wildland Fire Management wildfire suppression at the rates necessary to meet demand
claims.sourceSpan: may be apportioned up to the rate for operations necessary for wildfire suppression activities.

claims.claim: Section 118 covers SBA 7(a) [paragraphs (1)-(35)], 5(g), 503, and 303(b) commitments; Section 122 covers FEMA DRF Stafford Act response/recovery; Section 125 covers Interior and Forest Service Wildland Fire Management
claims.sourceSpan: for commitments to guarantee debentures under section 303(b) of the Small Business Investment Act of 1958

claims.claim: Continues TANF and Section 1108(b) of the Social Security Act through December 4, 2026 out of any money in the Treasury not otherwise appropriated
claims.sourceSpan: out of any money in the Treasury of the United States not otherwise appropriated, there are hereby appropriated such sums as may be necessary

claims.claim: Section 126 continues activities authorized by part A of title IV (other than under section 403(c) or 418) and section 1108(b) at FY2026 authority and manner through the section 106(3) date, appropriating such sums as may be necessary
claims.sourceSpan: Activities authorized by part A of title IV (other than under section 403(c) or 418) and section 1108(b) of the Social Security Act shall continue through the date specified in section 106(3), in the manner authorized for fiscal year 2026

claims.sourceSpan: there is appropriated

claims.claim: Section 127 appropriates $174,000 to Alfredia Scott (widow of David A. Scott, late a Representative from Georgia) and $174,000 to the heirs at law of Lindsey O. Graham (late a Senator from South Carolina); Section 128 blocks any adjustment under 2 U.S.C. 4501
claims.sourceSpan: for payment to Alfredia Scott, widow of David A. Scott, late a Representative from the State of Georgia, $174,000

claims.claim: Section 114 re-designates amounts previously designated as emergency/disaster-relief requirements as an emergency requirement under the FY2022 budget resolution and FY2027 House budget enforcement, and treats prior disaster-relief designations as continuing
claims.sourceSpan: is designated by the Congress as an emergency requirement pursuant to section 4001(a)(1) of S. Con. Res. 14 (117th Congress), the concurrent resolution on the budget for fiscal year 2022, and to legislation establishing fiscal year 2027 budget enforcement in the House of Representatives

claims.sourceSpan: to legislation establishing fiscal year 2027 budget enforcement in the House of Representatives

claims.claim: Section 115 permits rescissions/cancellations of discretionary budget authority continued under section 101 by reducing the rate for operations for the current applicable TAFS, capped at the lesser of the prior-Act amount or the balances available as of October 1, 2026
claims.sourceSpan: may be continued instead by reducing the rate for operations otherwise provided by section 101 for such current applicable TAFS
claims.note: Cap = lesser of amount specified in the applicable Act or balances available as of October 1, 2026 (Sec 115(b)).

claims.claim: OMB may reduce operating rates to absorb previously-scheduled rescissions, with an OMB report to the Appropriations Committees due November 20, 2026
claims.sourceSpan: No later than November 20, 2026, the Director of the Office of Management and Budget shall provide to the Committees on Appropriations of the House of Representatives and the Senate a comprehensive list of the rescissions or cancellations

claims.claim: Section 120 substitutes 2026 for 2025, 2027 for 2026, and 2028 for 2027 in Section 747 of title VII of division E of the FY2026 Financial Services and General Government Appropriations Act, and updates the underlying statutory reference
claims.sourceSpan: section 747 of title VII of division E of Public Law 119-75 shall be applied by
claims.note: Sec 101(5) confirms division E of PL 119-75 = FSGG Appropriations Act, 2026; year substitutions and citation update are Sec 120(a)(1)-(4).

claims.claim: The substitution advances the year references in the underlying provision by one year, but the CR does not restate the underlying provision
claims.sourceSpan: substituting
claims.note: Structural observation consistent with source; the CR only states the substitutions, not the underlying section 747 text.

claims.claim: The bill covers only 65 days (October 1 through December 4, 2026) and does not address what happens if full-year appropriations are not enacted by December 4, 2026
claims.sourceSpan: (3) December 4, 2026.
claims.note: Oct 1 through Dec 4, 2026 inclusive = 65 days (arithmetic on sourced Dec 4 date + FY2027 start). No provision addresses a post-Dec-4 lapse for discretionary accounts.

claims.claim: The bill funds IHS staffing for new facilities but does not include a similar anomaly for staffing at other federal health facilities opened during the same period
claims.sourceSpan: for an additional amount for costs of staffing and operating facilities that were opened, renovated, or expanded in fiscal years 2022, 2026, and 2027
claims.note: Analytical absence; only IHS staffing anomalies appear in source.

claims.claim: The bill extends NFIP authority via Section 121 but leaves the underlying transactional ceilings and borrowing authority unchanged
claims.sourceSpan: Sections 1309(a) and 1319 of the National Flood Insurance Act of 1968 (42 U.S.C. 4016(a) and 4026) shall be applied by substituting the date specified in section 106(3) of this Act for
claims.note: Sec 121 performs only a date substitution; no ceiling/borrowing change appears.

claims.claim: The bill continues TANF and mandatory payments through December 4, 2026 but does not address the treatment of monthly obligations due for periods after that date if the CR lapses
claims.sourceSpan: obligations for mandatory payments due on or about the first day of any month that begins after October 2026 but not later than 30 days after the date specified in section 106(3) may continue to be made
claims.note: Section 111(b) DOES address monthly mandatory-payment obligations after the covered period, allowing them up to 30 days after December 4, 2026. The gap overstates the silence; only obligations beyond that ~30-day window are unaddressed. Minor (buried in speculative gaps).

claims.claim: The bill blocks the Member COLA but does not address civilian federal employee pay adjustments that would otherwise take effect in January 2027
claims.note: Absence of a civilian pay-adjustment provision is accurate (Sec 112 only addresses furlough-avoidance apportionment), but the specific "January 2027" timing is extrinsic knowledge, not stated in source.

notes: Source audited = data/bill-text/119-HR-9770.txt, the Introduced-in-House (IH) text (18,128 chars); referencedSources is empty. Cache stage is "Passed House" with an Engrossed-in-House version dated 2026-07-21 that was NOT available as source text, so any Introduced->Engrossed deltas could not be checked; all analysis content claims verify against the IH text. No divisions[]. featured_quotes (Rep. Womack) is a Congressional Record quote with no CR source registered, so it was not claim-verified here. No material issues: every figure, account, entity, date, and direction in the bill-content prose matches source. Flags are all minor: WIC "up to" vs source "at" the rate (top_lines[2].subs[2]); gaps[3] contradicts Sec 111(b) which does provide a ~30-day post-expiration mandatory-payment window; extrinsic bits in likelihoodReason ("Chair of ... Appropriations Committee") and gaps[4] ("January 2027"); and four coverage omissions (Secs 109, 111(a), 111(b), 112 — standard CR mechanics incl. SNAP/Food and Nutrition Act continuation).
